# CareerAIR - rank every prospect, hide none
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

AC1. Every opportunity the scheduled email run acquires reaches the run's durable output with
     EITHER a fit score OR an explicit not-scored reason. Nothing is dropped. Where a requirement
     set was adopted, the score persists to careerair.fit_assessment as now. Where one was NOT
     adopted - and migration 016 then refuses the row - the state and its reason live in the email
     processing outcome detail process.mjs already writes. See B1.
AC2. The card NAMES items, ranked. Employer, role, score, blockers, link. Then the tail count and
     WHERE TO READ THE REST. A count where a list is required is a failure of this order.
     N = the top 10 SCORED items, plus ALL unscored and degraded items, which are not capped.
AC3. Unscored and degraded items sort ABOVE scored ones and appear FIRST on the card. "Err up where
     uncertain" applied to a null. These are the items most likely to matter and least likely to be
     read - the 2026-08-26 screening invitation that cost Warwick a live opportunity is exactly the
     shape that fails to score.
AC4. The label vocabulary is CLOSED, so AC1 is checkable:
     SCORED · SCORED-DEGRADED · UNSCORED-NO-EVIDENCE-CATALOGUE · UNSCORED-ZERO-ESSENTIALS ·
     UNSCORED-NO-ADVERT-TEXT · UNSCORED-ERROR
     DEGRADED IS DURABLE, not card-only - persist it via the existing note column on the assessment
     row so a fresh session cannot mistake a degraded 8 for a real one.
AC5. The 7/10 rule and calibration 2026-07-29.1 are UNCHANGED. The model tags; the code decides.
     What changes is only what happens to items below 7: they are shown, ranked lower. Nothing else.
AC6. Mutation-proven against the NEW defect class, which is HIDING, not failing to score. Four
     mutations, each RED with a non-zero executed count and a provably changed source, then restored
     GREEN: (a) a degraded row vanishes from the card; (b) an unscored row vanishes; (c) the renderer
     emits a count where a list is required; (d) the tail count is dropped.
AC7. NOT EXECUTABLE BY KEEL and must not be claimed: proven by a REAL SCHEDULED RUN producing a
     ranked, named card. Larry executes and evidences this. Capability is not automation.
# guidance: each independently checkable. If automatic, no AC may be satisfiable by a manual invocation of the delivered script alone.

## Sequencing

0. SETTLED ANSWERS to read-back #2, so nothing is invented at 200 lines in:

   B1 - CONFIRMED. Migration 016 refuses a fit_assessment row without an adopted requirement set,
   and the F4 cases never adopt one. So: fit_assessment rows are written ONLY where a set was
   adopted. The unscored state and its reason live in the EMAIL PROCESSING OUTCOME DETAIL. No DDL,
   no Silas decision, no migration. Your reading was right.

   B2 - CONFIRMED, and take it. Nulls sort UP. Unscored and degraded appear at the TOP of the card.

   B3 - ANSWERED. The tail points at a board the run writes itself:
   `C:/.fusion247/private/careerair/runtime/board/` is now in machine_surface. Write one
   human-readable ranked board per run, every acquired item on it, and have the card name that path.
   Do NOT write to runtime/applications/OPPORTUNITIES-BOARD.md - a scout agent owns that file and
   two writers is corruption. Convergence of the two boards is later work and is Larry's.

   N4 - CONFIRMED, take your recommendation. Leave journey.mjs's zero-essentials block INTACT for
   drafting - drafting from a defective requirement set spends money and produces a bad CV, which is
   Warwick's own priority (b). Surface it on the board as UNSCORED-ZERO-ESSENTIALS, at the top.

   N6 - ACCEPTED. There is no tests/journey suite. Keep the journey.mjs edit a pure substitution
   with identical behaviour, characterise the extracted unit from tests/email/, and say plainly in
   the return that journey.mjs's end-to-end path was not exercised by you.

1. Read-back if anything above is still unsettled. Otherwise build.
2. M2 extraction first: one new file in src/journey/ holding the composition, plus the smallest
   possible edit to journey.mjs that calls it.
3. AC1 - the gate runs in the pipeline, persisting where the schema allows and to the outcome detail
   where it does not.
4. AC2/AC3/AC4 - the board file, then the card that names from it.
5. AC6 - the four hiding-mutations.
6. Return diff and evidence to Larry. Do not commit, do not push. AC7 is Larry's.
